editorial:
Imagine your kid brings home a paper from a time capsule that lists every major disaster for the next fifty years, including the ones that haven't happened yet. That's the wild setup you get in this sci-fi thriller, where a teacher stumbles onto a list of numbers that turn out to be dates and death tolls. As he digs deeper, he realizes the predictions are coming true, and his own family might be tied to the final, terrifying entry. The movie mixes tense mystery with big disaster scenes, and it keeps you guessing about whether fate can be changed or if everything is already written.

The acting is solid, especially the lead performance, and the pacing rarely slows down once the clues start falling into place. Some moments feel a bit over the top, and the ending goes in a strange direction that won't work for everyone. Still, if you enjoy puzzle-driven thrillers with a sci-fi edge, this is a fun ride. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the teacher realizes the last prediction points to a massive solar flare that will wipe out Earth. He sends his son and a friend's daughter away with mysterious strangers who turn out to be aliens, taking the children to a new planet. The teacher stays behind and watches the world end as the flare hits. The twist is that the numbers were never meant to save everyone, just to prepare a chosen few for a fresh start.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves puzzle-driven thrillers with a sci-fi edge.
